missions.title: Premium glass NIGHT/DAY visual system
missions.scope: One canonical token layer for both themes, a generated night material bridge over the renderer's hard-coded navy literals, and a single glass material pass applied across all 14 application sections; type, focus, elevation, state, RTL, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-colours behaviour included.
missions.ui: Obsidian-violet night and porcelain-violet day authored as one token pair; 624 hard-coded navy surface literals re-mapped to canonical roles by a generated, checked bridge; one glass recipe (translucent layered fill + 20px blur + saturate + luminous top edge + three elevation tiers) applied to shell, heroes, panels, cards, inspectors, workbenches and dialogs; Plus Jakarta Sans / Tajawal / JetBrains Mono replace the pinned Arial and Segoe UI; focus, kbd, table heads, rows, scrollbars and footer strip unified; reduced-transparency, reduced-motion and forced-colors guards added.
missions.nativeProvider: not-applicable (material layer only; no provider or measurement changed)
missions.persistence: Existing knoux_theme_preference / knoux_theme persistence in NavigationContext is unchanged and still drives the resolved theme.
missions.securityConsent: No new capability, permission, file access, registry or account contact. Screenshots and performance samples use an isolated Electron profile against disposable fixtures; owner files, clipboard and OS state untouched. Two security-adjacent findings were recorded rather than silently patched: an inert Settings accent control and a frame-ancestors CSP declared in a meta tag where Chromium ignores it, with a workflow comment claiming a response header that does not exist.

missions.notes: CHECKPOINT, not MISSION_COMPLETE.
